answer: An agent economy can tie each key to bonded storage it must prove it holds. Every key keeps its own saffron shard, a unique 2 GB replica, and a falcon audit hits all keys at once with random blocks and a 1-second deadline; keys whose reply times show one disk serving several replicas are grouped, and the k-th key on a shared disk locks 15×k² POA. A lone key locks 15, ten clones 5,775 in all, 1,000 about 5 billion, versus ~0.43M minted each epoch. A failed audit slashes the bond; a tundra tier lets idle keys freeze shards cheaply but earn nothing. Weakness: fast SSD arrays mask sharing.
